The skip comes after the diagnostic, not before it.","citations":[{"file":"src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs","side":"new","startLine":1005,"endLine":1009,"quote":"continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member."}]},{"statement":"The analyzer therefore reports the problem instead of failing.","verdict":"supported","claimIds":["c7","c8"],"explanation":"c7 and c8 show tests that expect MsgPack005 for duplicate and mixed keys, with no analyzer failure.","citations":[]},{"statement":"I added analyzer tests for missing keys, AllowPrivate, duplicate keys and mixed key kinds, plus two execution tests: no formatter is generated for a suppressed type, and it round-trips through the dynamic resolver.","verdict":"supported","claimIds":["c5","c6","c7","c9"],"explanation":"c6 covers missing keys and AllowPrivate, c7 covers duplicate and mixed keys, and c9 also covers AllowPrivate. c5 shows that the generated resolver returns no formatter and that the type round-trips with the Standard options, whose resolver falls back to the dynamic resolver.","citations":[]},{"statement":"The README gains a section on opting out of source generation and lists which diagnostics still apply.","verdict":"supported","claimIds":["c4"],"explanation":"c4 shows the new 'Opting out of source generation' section, which lists the diagnostics that still apply and those that are not reported.","citations":[]}]}
